question: Does the existing rule-only static-v2 material profile keep a positive finite served-candidate W-L advantage over unfitted uniform material on newly generated free_random / asymmetric-movement rules?
changed_premise: Mature-static positive Static-Unit evidence exists only on four bilateral classic_like TRAIN rules; asymmetric movement plus free setup is a distinct mechanism class inside the stated generic domain.

rules.policy: Generate in seed order; if a seed raises GenerationError, record the failure and take the next fallback seed, keeping six rules. Rule dicts and sha256 frozen in rules.json before any game outcome.

families.policy: Fitness-blind deterministic prefixes: random.Random(gs*1000000+index) chooses among sorted-repr legal actions; keep the first 32 prefixes that are still ongoing after 4 plies; record every attempt including terminals.

foe_construction.fixed_random99031_channels: first channel weight 1.0 then random.Random(99031).uniform(0.5,1.5) per remaining channel in sorted channel order; frozen here before outcomes, explicitly NOT the AUX random99031 vector (different channel space)

reuse: Unit vs uniform is paid once per rule/family at owner 0 and reused as the opposite-role logical cell with sign flip; all other label/foe/owner combinations are paid separately.
statistics: Paired candidate-minus-unit differences; UNKNOWN reward contributes [-1,+1]*|coefficient| so every interval is finite and explicit. Pooled envelope from 2000 within-rule family-group resamples (conditional on the six fixed rules). Per-rule intervals reported separately.
decision: Positive vs zero-containing/reversing per-rule intervals on this new mechanism class; no population, equivalence, best-seed or unique-price claim.
scope: One bounded served-candidate diagnostic on six fixed generated rules. No fit, learner, optimizer, AUX checkpoint or AUX-side state; UNKNOWN and failures retained; caps not extended.
